stem: A postoperative client who is physically dependent on opioids develops opioid-induced respiratory depression. Which naloxone strategy is most appropriate?

options.A: Give a large IV bolus to produce immediate complete reversal of all opioid effects
options.B: Titrate small IV doses to restore adequate ventilation and alertness while avoiding unnecessary complete reversal
options.C: Withhold naloxone because physical opioid dependence is a contraindication
options.D: Use the same fixed dose regardless of the client's response or opioid dependence

rationale: Naloxone labeling directs that postoperative opioid-induced respiratory depression be treated with smaller IV doses titrated to adequate ventilation and alertness without significant pain or discomfort. The label also warns that abrupt complete reversal in a person physically dependent on opioids may precipitate acute withdrawal.
educational_objective: Use titrated naloxone dosing for postoperative opioid respiratory depression and avoid unnecessary abrupt complete reversal in clients physically dependent on opioids.
source_document_title: Naloxone Hydrochloride Injection, USP — Prescribing Information
source_locator: Warnings > Drug Dependence; Dosage and Administration > Usage in Adults > Postoperative Opioid-Induced Depression
source_claim_supported: Naloxone should be used cautiously in opioid-dependent patients because abrupt complete reversal can precipitate withdrawal; postoperative respiratory depression is treated with smaller IV doses titrated to adequate ventilation and alertness without significant pain or discomfort.
correction_summary: Final reaudit changed opioid-tolerant to physically dependent on opioids so the withdrawal warning exactly matches the label. The response-based postoperative naloxone titration endpoint is unchanged.
audit_findings: B uniquely matches the label. A risks excessive/abrupt reversal; C is false because physical dependence is a caution rather than a contraindication; D contradicts response-based titration. No second answer remains.
